the mechanism of action of cholera enterotoxin.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the A and B chains of heat-labile toxin are periplasmic proteins.
the A and B components of heat-labile toxin are both located in the periphery of the cell.
heat-labile enterotoxicity is a periplasmic property, and that the A and B polypeptide subunits of heatlabile enterotoxin are located in the cytoplasm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
enterotoxin from E. coli is a periplasmic toxin.
enterotoxin does not form aggregates in phosphate buffers, but that the toxin forms aggregates in Tris buffers.
enterotoxin, in the presence of EDTA, is located in the perplasm and forms aggregates which are not associated with the cell membrane.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the toxin is not membrane associated and that it is not a virulence factor for E. coli.
the enterotoxin is not associated with the inner or outer membranes of E. coli.
enterotoxin should be isolated from E. coli in buffers that contain high salt concentrations.
